newsitem.title: CHINA: Loral to sign China satellite deal.
newsitem.headline: Loral to sign China satellite deal.

text.p: U.S. satellite maker Space Systems/Loral Inc said it would on Friday formally sign a contract to build a $200 million communications satellite for China Telecommunications Broadcast Satellite Corp (Chinasat).
"The package is about $200 million and our portion of that is $100 million," said president of Loral Asia Pacific Henry Stackpole of the contract to build the high-powered Chinasat 8 orbiter.

Space Systems/Loral, a unit of Loral Space & Communications Ltd, would provide Chinasat with an 11,000-watt satellite operating on both C- and Ku-band frequencies to be put in orbit in late 1998, Stackpole said.

The satellite would begin providing video, data and digital services from 1999, with 16 Ku-band channels at 125 watts per channel and 36 C-band channels at 37 watts each allowing communications coverage to all of China.
"It is the most powerful satellite that China has purchased so far," Stackpole said, adding that the contract would be signed with Chinasat at Beijing's Great Hall of the People on Friday afternoon.
Chinasat 8 would have a mission life of 15 years, Loral said.

Chinasat, which is controlled by China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, had not yet made public its choice of launcher for Chinasat 8 and had not released its business plan for the satellite, he said.
"The decision (on launcher) has not yet been made," Stackpole said.
